ALEX (`who:alex`), relayed by Anthony 2026-08-14 as five written notes — the THIRD report from the second user, after `fact:second-user-report-2026-08-11` and `fact:second-user-first-run-report-2026-08-13`.

⭐⭐ THIS NODE RECORDS THE TWO NOTES THAT ARE NOT IDEAS: THEY DESCRIBE DEFECTS ALREADY FIXED ON MAIN. That is the finding, and it answers a question the previous fact node left explicitly open.

═══ 1. THE SETTINGS UPSERT — CLOSED, AND NOW MEASURED BY RUNNING IT, NOT BY READING CODE ═══

HIS WORDS: *"`reflow2 init .` should upsert `settings.local.json` (or whatever settings file is relevant for the agent harness) instead of replacing it."*

✅ MEASURED 2026-08-14 by running `tools/reflow2_init.py` on HEAD (`cbb1a19`) against a scratch project holding a settings file the USER owns — 4-space indent, their own `permissions` block, their own `Stop` hook:
```
permissions identical  : True      (byte-for-byte)
their own Stop hook    : survived  (reflow2's registered as a SECOND group)
indent preserved       : True      (4-space in, 4-space out)
diff                   : 38 changed lines, 0 REMOVALS — purely additive
21 -> 59 lines, entirely from reflow2's four hook-event registrations
```
⇒ **IT IS A GENUINE UPSERT ON HEAD.** Nothing removed, nothing reformatted. The original defect was never an overwrite — `ensure_hooks` always merged — it was that the whole file came back re-serialised at a fixed 2-space indent, making a merge INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A REWRITE in `git diff`. `detected_indent(raw)` closed that, and the run above confirms it end to end.

⚠️ THE ONE RESIDUAL, recorded because it is what a user actually sees and it is not a defect: a 21-line file becomes 59. The growth is real content — four hook events in verbose JSON — not reformatting, and zero lines are removed. But a first-time reader watching their small file nearly triple may still read it as being taken over, which is the same PERCEPTION problem the indent fix was aimed at rather than a separate bug.

═══ 2. THE MISSING SHAREABLE ARTIFACT — CLOSED IN PR #172 ═══

HIS WORDS: *"I wasn't sure where the graph artifact was (reflow2-export.json) … none of them were the graph json file that could be committed to a repo and pulled down and utilized by another project member."*

✅ FIXED in PR #172 (`fadc197`, 2026-08-13), and confirmed by the same scratch run above, which reported: *"docs/design/upsert-probe.json (CREATED — the shareable design record. .reflow2/ is machine state and ignored; THIS is the file to commit)"*. `write_shareable_export` now ALWAYS writes it, including on a brand-new project: an empty export is a real document (stamp, `graph_id`, `content_hash`, zero nodes) and committing it means the first real export CHAINS FROM IT.

═══ 🛑 SO THE STANDING QUESTION IS ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER MATTERS MORE THAN EITHER FIX ═══

`fact:second-user-first-run-report-2026-08-13` ended with: *"NOT RULED OUT: that Alex is on an OLDER kit … His version was not established. Ask before concluding."* **Two of five notes describing behaviour that no longer exists — both now reproduced as WORKING on HEAD — makes the older-kit reading the strong one.** The alternative, that both fixes are ineffective in the field, is now measured against and did not hold locally.

⚠️ CONSEQUENCE FOR HOW HIS REPORTS ARE READ: a report from an old kit is still a true report about the version he ran, and it is NOT evidence about HEAD. Every idea captured from this batch was therefore measured against HEAD before being recorded.

⇒ **ASK HIM WHAT VERSION HE IS RUNNING, AND WHETHER UPDATING WORKED.** The gap between what shipped and what a real user is running is itself unmeasured, and `user-iterative-release-preference` states the goal as a ONE-WORD UPDATE. If the second user is releases behind while fixes for his own reports sit in main, **the update path is the defect** — and nothing currently reports it.

📌 THE LIVE HALF OF NOTE 1 IS THE PARENTHETICAL, not the upsert: *"(or whatever settings file is relevant for the agent harness)"* — reflow2 registers its loop nudge ONLY in `.claude/settings.local.json`. That is `dec:idea-the-loop-nudge-exists-for-one-harness-only`, and it is now downstream of `dec:idea-init-asks-which-harness-and-installs-only-that` (ACCEPTED 2026-08-14): once init ASKS which harness, the hook has an answer to follow.

📌 PATTERN, NOW THREE FOR THREE: every defect in the last increment was found by a first-time user or by running two real projects at each other — none by reading code, none by a gate. `dec:idea-feedback-collection-is-asked-once-and-recorded` — the mechanism ALEX ASKED FOR HIMSELF — remains unbuilt, which is why his findings keep arriving as a relayed email.
